text: The autoscaling review is closed, but Theo doesn't stop there. The same review pass is a natural moment to check the other piece of infrastructure that shipped around the same time: the AWS S3 backup bucket from Lesson Six.
Opening driftwood-outdoor-backups in the S3 console, the Permissions tab shows a banner that should never be ignorable: public access, not blocked, with a warning that objects can be public.

The bucket policy confirms why. The Principal field is a wildcard, meaning anyone, not just Driftwood's own AWS account, can read every object -- and S3 Block Public Access was never enabled to override that. The intent was only the replication job's IAM role.

This is exactly why the mistake survives: the bucket works perfectly fine for its intended purpose the whole time. Nothing breaks, nothing errors, and nobody has a reason to open the Permissions tab unless they go looking.
Two separate, confirmed findings now sit on Theo's list. Next lesson fixes both, and proves with real evidence that each fix actually worked.
